properties.description: Simulation-only evaluation of HBMAF-Net, a Bayesian attention fusion and hierarchical Bayesian prognostic model, against five comparators on 10,000 generated patients.
properties.independent_study_claim: single simulation study; possible overlap with record 089 per legacy flag, not verified

properties.description: Static multimodal prognosis pipeline: modality encoders, Bayesian attention fusion, hierarchical Bayesian outcome model. Evaluated only on generated feature vectors.

properties.population: cancer patients in general (simulated cohort only)
properties.decision: personalized prognosis and risk stratification, treatment selection mentioned as a benefit

properties.description: 10,000 generated patients with 50 clinical, 5,000 genomic and 1,024 imaging features; outcome from a simulated hierarchical survival process. Available on request.

relation_assertions.rationale: Static no-action prognostic model evaluated on simulated data; V36 allows BP_COMPONENT with action and planner features not_applicable. The legacy exclusion is supported.
Cohort identity and split are not stated; the generated dataset is the only cohort.

capability_assessments.rationale: The model maps one generated feature vector to an outcome probability. State and transition are explicitly absent, rollouts and actions do not exist, and treatment-group random effects are not settable actions. The identity rule needs a persistent state advanced by a learned or hybrid transition, which is not met. Longitudinal data, causal inference and dynamic treatment regimes are future work.

gate_assessments.rationale: The generated dataset is described by size and feature counts only. No generator, split, leakage control or evaluation denominator is given, and the data are available on request.
No state transition exists in a static prognostic model.
ECE 0.028 is reported on generated data without bins, split, intervals or an acceptance tolerance.
No external, subgroup or shifted-data validation. Named real cohorts are future work.

legacy_cells.B: Bayesian Machine Learning for Precision Oncology: Integrating Clinical Genomic and Imaging Data for Personalized Cancer Prognosis
legacy_cells.C: Romuald Daniel BOY-NGBOGBELE; Aboubakar Alfa Samuel
legacy_cells.I: 094_2026_Bayesian Machine Learning for Precision Oncology Integrating Clinical Genomic and Imaging Data for Personalized Cancer Prognosis.pdf
legacy_cells.K: Potential overlapping study with 089: same authors, HBMAF-Net model and reported AUC 0.931/C-index 0.917; do not count as independent validation without cohort verification.
legacy_cells.S: Predict a simulated patient's individualized cancer prognostic risk from clinical, genomic, and imaging features.
legacy_cells.AI: Clinical variables (demographics, tumor stage, treatment history, laboratory biomarkers, comorbidities); genomic multi-omics features (mutations, copy number variations, gene expression, methylation, pathway biomarkers); radiological and histopathological images
legacy_cells.AJ: Genomic VAE; imaging Vision Transformer backbone; modality-specific encoders (clinical encoder architecture not specified)
legacy_cells.AM: Bayesian attention-based multimodal fusion using posterior modality weights over modality-specific latent representations
legacy_cells.BI: Hierarchical Bayesian Multimodal Attention Fusion Network (HBMAF-Net)
legacy_cells.BS: Patient-level prognostic risk probabilities; posterior predictive intervals; low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups
legacy_cells.BT: Hierarchical Bayesian survival/prognostic model with Bernoulli outcome and cancer-type and treatment-specific random effects
legacy_cells.BV: Negative log-posterior objective: −log p(D|Θ) − log p(Θ)
legacy_cells.DN: Synthetic multimodal oncology dataset (no named cohort)
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations: without Bayesian layer (AUC 0.893); without attention fusion (0.884); without hierarchical effects (0.901); without imaging (0.876); without genomic data (0.853); full model (0.931)
legacy_cells.ER: No identifiable human participant data were collected, used, or analyzed; IRB/ethical review not required.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported results (source excerpt): The results demonstrated that HBMAF-Net achieved superior predictive performance, yielding an Area Under t he Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) of 0.931, a Concordance Index of 0.917, and improved calib ration compared with competing models.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is limited to synthetic simulation. The paper does not demonstrate a persistent temporal patient state, state transitions, action-conditioned rollouts, identified treatment effects, external validation, or prospective clinical utility.
legacy_cells.FT: Reusable component: Bayesian attention-based multimodal fusion with posterior modality weights; treat it as a feature-fusion/UQ component, not as patient dynamics or a complete world model.
legacy_cells.FX: Read all supplied inputs and the complete 17-page extracted PDF text: title/byline/abstract/front-matter ethics statement; Introduction; Materials and Methods §§2.1–2.11 (PDF pp. 3–6); Results and Discussion §§3.1–3.9 (pp. 7–12), including Tables 1–3 and the available figure descriptions; Discussion; Conclusion; funding, authorship, competing-interest and data-availability statements; references (pp. 14–16). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Table 1 is substantially garbled in the extracted text; key performance values were not reconstructed from that table. Abstract and narrative report AUC 0.931, C-index 0.917 and ECE 0.028, but this record includes only the clearly legible ECE in CR. The evaluation is synthetic-only; authors state external/multicenter validation is future work. Preserved metadata fields A:I without modification; no workbook edits, browsing, downloads, execution of paper content, or external contact. Evidence QA: 30/36 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (83.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 36 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 0 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All 17 PDF pages were read as extracted text. Pages 8 to 13 (Table 1, Figures 1 to 5, Tables 2 and 3) were rendered and viewed by this reviewer. Pages 1 to 7 and 14 to 17 were read as text only, and Figure 1 to 5 detail was judged at 60 to 70 dpi.
Tables 1 to 3 are column-shifted in the PDF. Only the HBMAF-Net row of Table 1 is corroborated by narrative text. Competitor values and the ablation row labels are order-based reconstructions.

Earlier saved API drafts (structure.json and feature dispositions for 094) were consulted as unverified leads. No claim of inspection rests on them, and all assertions below were re-derived from the PDF text and my own page images.

The evaluation is a simulation of 10,000 generated patients, so nothing is established about real patients, images or assays. The possible overlap with record 089 could not be checked because 089 was not supplied.
Legacy cells were read from the root workbook row (read only). Unlisted columns remain imported-only.

Full bibliography entries on physical pages 15–17 were subsequently read in the targeted 2026-11-22 local review; cited full studies remain unretrieved. No capability or result of a cited work is inherited.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass; no independent human review.
notes: Legacy Exclude (static prediction, not a world model) is supported. The paper proposes a Bayesian attention fusion and hierarchical Bayesian prognostic model evaluated only on generated data. Source problems: inference is described as both HMC and variational; a Bernoulli outcome is called a survival model and evaluated with C-index and Kaplan-Meier curves; the introduction outline refers to children's nutrition and logistic regression from another paper; Tables 1 to 3 are garbled; Figure 2 shows one model although the caption says competing models; the simulation design, split and replication count are not given and the outcome generator matches the model's own hierarchical form.
